about.title: Personal Injury Help in Yuba City, California
about.longDescription: Yuba City sits at a crossroads of daily traffic, with corridors like Rt 20, Bridge Street, Rt 99, and Garden Highway carrying commuters, farm traffic, and through-travelers every day. In the most recent recorded year, Sutter County logged 254 injury collisions in and around the city, leaving 348 people hurt and 2 people dead. Many of these crashes cluster around Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when work traffic and weekend errands overlap. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, or in a fall, workplace incident, or another accident caused by someone else's carelessness, you may be wondering what comes next. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured people in Yuba City with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of what happened and explain your options. Attorneys in this network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. You don't have to figure this out alone or guess at deadlines; a quick, free conversation can help you understand where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you 2 years from the date of injury to file a claim, but if a government entity was involved, that window can shrink to as little as 6 months. Waiting too long can cost you the chance to recover anything.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages in typical injury cases, meaning compensation for pain and suffering isn't artificially limited.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in this network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you — reducing the financial risk of exploring your options.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have 2 years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury claim. If your injury involved a government entity or vehicle, that deadline can be as short as 6 months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Yuba City?
items.answer: Public crash records show higher collision counts along corridors such as Rt 20, Bridge Street, Rt 99, and Garden Highway, with reported crashes tending to peak on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are neutral public-record patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent personal injury attorneys. We don't provide legal representation ourselves.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Attorneys in this network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if they recover money on your behalf. There's no cost to start the conversation.
